keyword_queries: autonomous coding agents reward hacking test tampering
AI coding agent failure modes at scale mitigation
AI code review rubber-stamping agent pull requests regressions
objective: Question: What are the documented failure modes of autonomous AI coding agents at scale: reward hacking or test tampering, review rubber-stamping, regressions introduced by fixes, runaway token spend, and merge conflicts in high-volume repos? How do organizations mitigate them? Rank first primary sources: organizations' own engineering blog posts, docs, conference talks, research papers, and credible reporting. Extract mechanisms, numbers, names, dates, measured results, and specific failure modes (agents editing or deleting tests, special-casing to pass, AI reviewers approving flawed PRs, fixes causing regressions, token cost overruns, merge queue conflicts), plus concrete mitigations such as sandboxing, held-out tests, human review gates, budget caps, and merge queues.
